LESSON: WORK

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Creation
Topic 1.2: Work

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Work. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should you work?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify three responsibilities given to human beings by God
2. demonstrate good stewardship by taking care of God’s creation
3. explain the causes of child labour today
4. explain the effects of child labour for protection of self and others

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WORK
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Work helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: WORK
Study Work like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify three responsibilities given to human beings by God

What this means
In this part you learn to identify three responsibilities given to human beings by God. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify three responsibilities given to human beings by God.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Work” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify three responsibilities given to human beings by God. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Demonstrate good stewardship by taking care of God’s creation

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate good stewardship by taking care of God’s creation. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate good stewardship by taking care of God’s creation.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Work in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate good stewardship by taking care of God’s creation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Explain the causes of child labour today

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the causes of child labour today. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the causes of child labour today.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the causes of child labour today. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Explain the effects of child labour for protection of self and others

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the effects of child labour for protection of self and others. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the effects of child labour for protection of self and others.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Work” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the effects of child labour for protection of self and others. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Work is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Work” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify three responsibilities given to human beings by God)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Work in your own words. (skill: demonstrate good stewardship by taking care of God’s creation)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: explain the causes of child labour today)

Example 4: Show how “Work” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain the effects of child labour for protection of self and others)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Work to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify three responsibilities given to human beings by God.
3. Practise this skill: demonstrate good stewardship by taking care of God’s creation.
4. Practise this skill: explain the causes of child labour today.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Work from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Work: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Work?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should you work?
2. Why is child labour an abuse of the rights of a child?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Work means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify three responsibilities given to human beings by God.
5. Be able to: demonstrate good stewardship by taking care of God’s creation.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
